key_insight: VersaCamVLA makes robotic VLA policies work with changing camera setups by learning a camera-agnostic scene representation. This lets a single policy handle different numbers, poses, and placements of cameras more robustly.
problem_solved: Most VLA robotic manipulation models are trained with fixed camera configurations, so they break when cameras are added, removed, or moved at deployment. This paper addresses the brittleness of camera-dependent policies.
method: Learns a unified scene-token interface that converts an arbitrary set of posed RGB views into a shared representation.
Decouples camera-set encoding from action prediction so the policy is less tied to a specific sensor layout.
Supports variable camera count and pose at inference time while preserving manipulation performance.
impact: For practitioners, this means robotic policies can be deployed across different labs, robots, and setups without retraining for every camera arrangement. It improves robustness, flexibility, and real-world usability of VLA systems.
